topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of cellular transformation and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Discovery of transforming viruses, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the history of tumor virology led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the development of assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of cancer-associated genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the functional definitions of oncogenes and tumor suppressors and demonstrate how pathways like Rb and p53 govern cell cycle checkpoints and mutant phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the differences between sequence and chromosomal instability as well as the DNA repair, replication, and mitotic failures that cause them.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how stepwise mutation accumulation drives tumor evolution and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer closes the session, opens the floor to questions, and suggests supplemental reading material.
